title: The Singhs Would Steal Their Horses and Get Lost

blocks.text: The Afghan effort to pin down the Khalsa remains ineffective because the Singhs would steal their horses and get lost before any disciplined pursuit could catch them. Advisers warn that chasing Majhail Sikh bands through jungle and scrub will only exhaust imperial troops, who do not know the terrain and cannot survive long without secure water and supply.

This argument becomes a grudging acknowledgment of Khalsa resilience: the brave Majhail Singhs know how to disperse, reassemble, and strike again while stronger-looking armies blunder after them. The page therefore treats the question of how could the mighty Khalsa Panth be annihilated? as a real strategic dilemma rather than a boast.

At the same time, the Sikhs themselves decide they cannot preserve families and community merely by hiding. After organizing a religious congregation for this purpose, they move against Sirhind, force Jain Khan to fall back, camp near Malerkotla, and begin debating what their next step should be.
